query: Consider the following context: How to rationally design composition of alloys with desired properties has always been an open and challenging question, especially for high-entropy alloy (HEA) which has huge selections of composition due to the feature of multi-principal elements. Although great efforts have been made in the past decades, such as approaches based on thermo-kinetic analysis and simulations, strategies to quick determine the optimal HEA composition remain lacking. In that context, which method can be used for design intrinsically strong, ductile, and low-weight refractory HEA (RHEA) compositions, and why?

generation.hypothesis: A machine learning framework trained on integrated thermo-kinetic, simulation, and experimental data can rapidly identify refractory HEA compositions with intrinsically improved strength, ductility, and reduced weight compared to those designed by traditional methods.
generation.material_initial_state: A vast compositional space of multi-principal element refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) with diverse microstructures (mostly BCC solid solutions exhibiting severe lattice distortions).
generation.intervention: Development and deployment of a data-driven machine learning model that predicts intrinsic strength, ductility, and weight based on historical thermo-kinetic, simulation, and experimental datasets.
generation.conditions: Screening is performed in silico under typical ambient and elevated temperature conditions relevant to RHEA applications, with follow-up experimental validation.
generation.structural_mediator: Predicted microstructural features (e.g., lattice distortion and phase stability) that correlate with mechanical performance in RHEAs.
generation.mechanism: The ML model leverages patterns in multi-fidelity datasets to capture complex relationships between alloy composition and performance, rapidly narrowing down candidate compositions with the desired balance of properties.
generation.predicted_outcome: Selected RHEA compositions will exhibit significantly higher intrinsic strength and ductility while maintaining a lower alloy density compared to alloys identified via conventional thermo-kinetic and simulation methods.
generation.baseline: Traditional design strategies based on exhaustive thermo-kinetic analyses and high-throughput simulations that require extensive computational resources and time.
generation.boundary: The approach is likely most effective within well-sampled regions of the compositional space; predictions for compositions at the extreme ends or with sparse training data may remain uncertain.
generation.uncertainty: The accuracy of predictions may be limited by the completeness and quality of available datasets, and potential model extrapolation issues in underrepresented compositional regimes.

falsification_experiment.design: Develop the proposed machine learning model using existing thermo-kinetic, simulation, and experimental data for RHEAs. Use the model to predict a set of optimal compositions. Fabricate these candidate alloys and subject them to standardized mechanical tests (e.g., tensile testing for strength and ductility, density measurements) under relevant temperatures. Compare the mechanical performance and weight of these alloys with those identified by traditional design methods.
measurements: Yield strength and ultimate tensile strength
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the experimental measurements of the ML-predicted alloys do not show statistically significant improvements in both strength and ductility, while also achieving lower density relative to alloys chosen by conventional methods, then the hypothesis will be falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Materials with high performance both at room and elevated temperatures are very attractive for a wide range of critical applications, potentially for aero-engine and fusion reactors [1] – [4] . For decades, ultra-strong, ductile, and heat-resistant materials have long been sought by the materials community, such as tungsten-based heavy alloys and nickel-based superalloys [3] , [5] . However, achieving alloys with an ultrahigh strength (>2 GPa) and a sufficient ductility (>10%) has presented a long-standing challenge. This has spurred significant research into metallurgical strategies to tailor microstructures for improved properties. One classical design paradigm is utilizing dilute concentrations of alloying elements, such as Re, Ti, and Cr, to improve the properties of W-based alloys; however, the “strength-ductility trade-off” has proven to be difficult to be solved with such single principal-element alloy systems due to the problem of brittle W-enriched phases with body-centered cubic (bcc) structures [5] , [6] . The concept of HEAs provides us an unprecedented degree of freedom in the design of advanced alloys with promising properties. For the rapid exploration of the vast compositional space and investigation of the composition and temperature effects on the microstructure, advanced HEA-design strategies and efficient tools are necessary. At present, a few advanced HEA-design strategies were reported by combining the physicochemical criteria, CALPHAD, data mining, and multi-objective optimization algorithm [21] , [22] , [35] – [37] , demonstrating that the CALPHAD method has played an important role in the design of advanced HEAs. There are two essential requirements to carry out calculations, using the CALPHAD method: computational software and database.
